Figure 1:\CaptionLeadOverview of OneWM.
A VAE encodes frames into latents; the observed prefix remains clean,
and the video expert denoises future latents. Action chunks are embedded for the action
expert. Causal joint attention couples the two experts, each receiving
instructionℓ\ellthrough its own text cross-attention
(Sec.3.2). The lower panels illustrate all-clean,
clean-prefix/noisy-suffix, and all-noisy action construction, unifying
world prediction and action generation (Sec.3.3).

Figure 2:\CaptionLeadEvaluation tasks and environments. We evaluate OneWM
on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboCasa365 in simulation, and on three real-world
tasks: block stacking, block insertion, and breakfast arrangement.

Figure 4:\CaptionLeadMain-camera world predictions.
Six cases from LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus compare GT, OneWM, and the
indicated world-model baseline. Orange boxes mark the regions enlarged
att+32t+32in each panel’s final column.

Figure 5:\CaptionLeadWrist-camera world predictions.
Six matched comparisons emphasize object position, shape, and pose near
the gripper. Each final column enlarges the same marked region att+32t+32for all three rows.

Figure 6:RoboCasa365 world predictions.Six matched cases
compare GT, OneWM,WM, andWMAdaLNfrom left (a,b),
wrist (c,d), and right (e,f) cameras. The final column enlarges the
same marked region att+16t+16for all four rows.

Figure 7:\CaptionLeadEndless dream on LIBERO.
Six rollouts generated by alternating action prediction and
action-conditioned world prediction. Each panel shows main- and
wrist-camera views; blue outlines mark the initial observations,
and every later frame is generated. Columns indicate modeled time,
with the final column showing the end of round 16.
